newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela aluminium companies lose $272 mln in '96.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela aluminium companies lose $272 mln in '96.

text.p: Three of the four companies in Venezuela's aluminum sector, due to be privatized this year, made losses in 1996 totaling some 130 billion bolivars ($272 million) due to the burden of debt servicing and foreign exchange losses, leading daily El Universal reported.

The newspaper gave results for only three of Venezuela's four companies related to aluminum production. All three posted operating profits, but only one of them, smelter Venalum, was able to turn a net profit. The other two saw their operating income levelled by debt and forex liabilities, the report said.
Bauxite producer Bauxilum made a net post-tax loss of 60 billion bolivars after an operating profit of 49 billion bolivars. Bauxite is the ore used to make aluminium.
Smelter Alcasa made a net loss of 84 billion bolivars along with operating income of 19 billion bolivars.
Venalum made a 13 billion bolivar net profit on operating profits of 90 billion bolivars, Pablo Morales, president of the three companies, told El Universal.

Officials at state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG), which groups those firms, and Venezuela's privatization agency, the National Investment Fund (FIV), were not available to comment on the results.
But Felix Duarte, chief accountant for the three companies, said audited results would be available by the end of the week.

According to CVG projections obtained by Reuters late last year, Bauxilum was forecast to make a 20 billion bolivar net loss in 1996 versus a 63 billion loss in 1995, while Alcasa was forecast making a 31 billion bolivar net loss versus a 59 billion bolivar loss the year before.
Venalum -- the jewel in the crown -- was seen making a 24 billion bolivar net profit, up from eight billion in 1995.

Profits at the sector's fourth company, carbon anode producer Carbonorca, were meanwhile seen rising to one billion bolivars from 872 million the year before. Carbonorca's results were not included in the newspaper report.

A controlling stake in the four-company block is due to be sold in the second half of the year, following Congressional discussion of the privatization contracts. About a dozen companies from Canada, the United States, Australia, Japan and Norway have shown interest in purchasing a 70 percent stake.
